extracted.intended_audience: academics and scholarly publishers (mathematicians, journal editors, and open-access advocates)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for creating and running an editor-owned arXiv-overlay, open-access mathematics journal — covering model choice, costs, presentation, peer review coordination, and publication workflow. Targeted at academics considering starting/operating such journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-owned open-access journal model
rubrics_metrics.description: Academics can publish journals of the highest quality without a commercial entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interview argues that journals need not be run by commercial publishers; an editor-owned model can provide high-quality publishing while avoiding harmful subscription fees. This is presented as both principled (resisting commercial costs) and practical (achievable using existing infrastructure).

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv overlay architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are submitted and hosted via the preprint server arXiv first; the journal performs refereeing services but doesn’t actually publish articles, it links to them on the arXiv preprint server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an arXiv-overlay reduces hosting/publishing costs and leverages existing preprint infrastructure. The overlay coordinates peer review and points readers to the arXiv version rather than rehosting content.

rubrics_metrics.name: No cost to reader or author
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish via Scholastica with no cost to reader or author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrete Analysis aims to have zero author or reader charges if possible. Costs are minimized by using overlay model and platforms such as Scholastica. If necessary for sustainability, only a very small submission fee (e.g., $10) may be charged to cover software costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal/alternative funding for sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover all journal costs using a small grant from the University of Cambridge; if funds run out, a tiny submission fee is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer institutional support or small grants rather than APCs or subscriptions. The model demonstrates feasibility of keeping costs minimal (contrast with APCs or expensive publisher models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-written paper descriptions to aid discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper will have a description on the journal’s website, written by the editors, that will explain the paper and why it’s worth reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing editorial summaries makes the website more browse-able and helps readers decide what to read; this is a deliberate differentiator from other overlay journals and publisher sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality online reading experience
rubrics_metrics.description: An online reading experience can be as high quality as print; a good website can make a journal appear high-quality without physical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in a well-designed website (e.g., through Scholastica) that is easy to navigate and visually appealing. Avoid assuming print format confers quality; instead, provide a polished online interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling publication (no issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not divide articles into issues; use a rolling publication model — whenever a paper’s accepted, publish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing immediately upon acceptance avoids artificial delays, embraces the internet’s affordances, and rejects mimicry of print-era constraints. Anti-pattern: waiting for 'issues' simply because of historical print practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review coordination as an essential function
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal coordinates peer-review (refereeing services) even though it does not rehost articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlay journals must still provide rigorous editorial and refereeing processes; the administrative coordination of peer review is a core service the journal supplies to ensure quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding APC model for mathematics when inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Article-processing charge (APC) model is often inappropriate and hostile for many mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although APCs can replace subscriptions financially, they may face strong opposition in mathematics; seek alternative cost models (editor-owned overlays, grants, tiny submission fees) rather than assuming APCs are the right solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of platforms that make setup/maintenance easy
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose tools (e.g., Scholastica) that allow the journal to be set up quickly and maintained without excessive overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier attempts at overlays were difficult to create and run; leveraging existing publishing/peer-review platforms reduces technical and administrative barriers to launching a journal.
